title: Agilus Diagnostics hosts Secretary of State for Scotland to explore diagnostic technology collaboration
summary: British Deputy High Commission Mumbai-facilitated visit showcases Microbira’s rapid microbial testing technology and opportunities for India–Scotland collaboration
thbAction: Pitch THB's diagnostics CRM to help labs manage doctor outreach, collection-center expansion, and B2B referral relationships while improving conversion and retention.
contentHtml:
British Deputy High Commission Mumbai-facilitated visit showcases Microbira’s rapid microbial testing technology and opportunities for India–Scotland collaboration 

Agilus Diagnostics hosted Douglas Alexander, Secretary of State for Scotland, and an accompanying Scottish delegation at its Goregaon facility in Mumbai. Facilitated by the British Deputy High Commission Mumbai, the visit showcased Agilus’s laboratory capabilities and explored opportunities for collaboration in diagnostic technology and research.

The programme included an overview of Agilus’s business and laboratory network, discussions on Edinburgh-based Microbira Limited’s plans for India, a demonstration of its rapid microbial testing technology and a walkthrough of Agilus’s Microbiology Department, where the technology is installed.

Rapid microbial testing can help identify microorganisms responsible for infections and detect antimicrobial resistance (AMR), supporting more timely and informed treatment decisions.

Vijender Singh, MD & CEO, Agilus Diagnostics, said: “India’s diagnostics sector presents significant opportunities for growth and innovation. Engagements with international technology companies can help bring advanced capabilities to India and assess their relevance to local healthcare needs. This visit was an opportunity to showcase Agilus’s capabilities and explore potential areas of collaboration.”

The Scotland Office has highlighted a potential £10 million export opportunity for Microbira in the Indian diagnostics market. This reflects the potential for UK diagnostic technology companies to expand their presence in India. The commercial scope of any potential collaboration involving Agilus Diagnostics, including investment commitments, has not been finalised.

Douglas Alexander, Secretary of State for Scotland, said: “India and Scotland have an opportunity to work together on antimicrobial resistance through research and innovation. The visit to Agilus Diagnostics showcased the potential of rapid microbial testing technology and the scope for collaboration to help tackle infections faster.”

Dr Deepak Sanghavi, Senior Vice President Operations & Chief of Mumbai Reference Lab, Agilus Diagnostics said: “The visit enabled us to showcase our microbiology capabilities and discuss the potential of emerging technologies. Collaboration with international innovators can help evaluate solutions that meet clinical needs while maintaining the quality and operational rigour required for diagnostic testing at scale.”

Separately, Agilus Diagnostics hosted nine UK diagnostics companies at its Goregaon facility on 26 October 2026 under the UK–India Diagnostic Cohort programme, providing an opportunity to showcase its laboratory capabilities and explore potential areas of collaboration.

Through such engagements, Agilus Diagnostics aims to strengthen dialogue with international technology innovators and explore opportunities to advance diagnostic capabilities in India.
